To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of CD56/ NCAM in bone marrow biopsies is useful in the differential diagnosis between neoplastic and reactive plasmacytic infiltration, since it is expressed by neoplastic but not by reactive plasma cells.
CD56/NCAL expression can be used to differentiate polyclonal plasma cell infiltrates from neoplastic ones in bone marrow biopsies.
CD56/NCAML is not expressed by reactive polyclonal plasmacytes, but it is by myeloma-associated neoplastic plasma cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohistological evaluation of 95 bone marrow plasmacytotic processes, which we have compared with 10 plasma cell myelomas.
the immunohistochemical characterization of polyclonality in BM reactive plasmacytic proliferations, as well as the usefulness of this approach in the differential diagnosis of PCM versus MGUS.
the phenotypic evaluation of reactive and neoplastic plasmas, with the aim to provide a more precise diagnostic approach in the study of bone marrow trephines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BM reactive plasmacytic proliferations are CD56/NCAL negative and cyclin D1 negative.

the immunohistochemical profile of polyclonal PC is CD138+/CD56-/-/cyclinD1- and that of neoplastic PC is CD138+/-/CD56+/cyclinD1+/-; the latter is also characterized by a monoclonal light chain restriction.
BM reactive plasmacytes are CD56/NCAL negative, whereas PCM-associated plasmacytes show a variable CD56/NCAML positivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD56/NCAL immunohistochemistry is a useful tool to differentiate reactive from malignant PC infiltrates.
BM reactive plasmacytic hyperplasias can be distinguished from neoplastic PCM by the presence of CD56/CD138 double-positive PCs, which are not found in reactive plasmacytoses.
the absence of CD56 immunoreactivity, together with the polyclonal pattern of light chain expression, is a reliable feature for the exclusion of a PCM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of cyclin D1 in a plasmacytic population should always raise the suspicion of PCM, even in the absence of monoclonal immunoglobulin expression.
the presence of cyclin D1 and CD56/NCAL expression in BM trephine biopsies is highly suggestive of PCM.
CD56/NCAL immunostaining is an important marker for distinguishing neoplastic from reactive PC infiltrations in the BM.
